subject: Fjord Analytics — IP & Feedback License: procurement timeline and redline ownership
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@fjordanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify IP / training rights in MSA + order form (Fjord)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Fjord is keen to progress. Procurement has a couple of stickier items on IP and training:

- We need explicit language that Fjord retains ownership of outputs generated from our customer data.
- Any use of Fjord data for model training must be opt-in and scoped via the Order Form (no broad feedback license).
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an explicit carveout for customer content from any persistent training use?

We attached a short SOW and a redline from our legal team (see attachments). Procurement wants a timeline: we need the MSA and Order Form agreed by Aug 9 to hit our quarter close. Can your legal team review the redlines and confirm whether any of these are deal blockers?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Ops, Fjord Analytics
Attachment: Fjord_SOW_v3.pdf

-----
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Liu <emma@fjordanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify IP / training rights in MSA + order form (Fjord)

Hi Emma — appreciate the clarity and the timeline. Quick summary from our side:

- Redwood’s baseline position is that customers retain ownership of their input data and customer-specific outputs. We typically offer customers an explicit opt-in for model training/feedback that is surfaced on the Order Form.
- The MSA contains a feedback license that is intended to allow Redwood to improve service quality, but we can narrow the scope for Fjord so it only applies to anonymized telemetry and not user content unless Fjord opts into training.

I’ve attached a suggested redline (fjord_msa_redlines.docx) that:
- Adds an ‘Order Form Opt‑In for Training’ clause (training requires explicit checkbox + SOW).
- Carveouts: customer content and outputs are excluded from our training corpus unless the Order Form states otherwise.
- Adds a short audit/telemetry note: we can provide aggregated telemetry but won’t use raw outputs for training.

Could Marissa / Neha help confirm whether the proposed wording creates any operational or SLA issues (billing, telemetry, or encryption constraints)? Also, does Redwood need SOC 2 evidence to satisfy Fjord’s procurement checklist — if so, we should surface that now.

Next steps: Mary/Neha to confirm internal sign-off and then submit the tracked redline back to Emma + Aaron (Fjord legal). If there are material changes to the feedback license language that affect unit economics, we’ll flag procurement.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: fjord_msa_redlines.docx

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Emma Liu <emma@fjordanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify IP / training rights in MSA + order form (Fjord)

Thanks Karthik — reviewed the suggested wording and added a few operational clarifications. High level notes:

1) Training opt-in language (Order Form):
- Proposed: "Customer may opt-in to allow Redwood to use Customer Data and Customer Outputs to improve models, solely as set forth in the applicable Order Form and associated SOW. Unless expressly opted-in, Redwood will not incorporate Customer Data or Customer Outputs into model training datasets."
- Rationale: keeps MSA clean but binding; Order Form drives the behavior.

2) Output ownership carveout:
- Proposed: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Outputs and to Data provided by Customer. Redwood shall not claim any ownership in Outputs or Customer Data."

3) Telemetry & aggregated signals:
- We can agree to allow Redwood to collect aggregated, non-identifiable system metrics for performance and bug fixes. Add explicit prohibition on using raw Outputs for training without opt-in.

4) Evidence / compliance:
- We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and can deliver a short evidence pack (data-handling, KMS, retention) to Fjord Procurement. This usually clears procurement questions quickly.

5) Commercial impact:
- If Fjord wants training opt-in on their Order Form, productization/time-to-market for a bespoke training pipeline can add ~6–8 weeks and incremental cost. We should flag any price adjustments; procurement should expect a pricing delta for training services (model retrain, fine-tuning, dataset ops).

I’ve tracked the above into the attached redline and noted the clauses that Sales should confirm with Pricing. If Neha confirms SOC 2 evidence and Pricing confirms delta, we can send back a clean redline to Emma/Aaron with an annotated procurement timeline.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: fjord_msa_redlines.docx (tracked)
Attachment: procurement_questions.xlsx

-----
From: Emma Liu <emma@fjordanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Aaron Blake (Legal) <aaron@fjordanalytics.com>, Fjord Procurement <procureops@fjordanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify IP / training rights in MSA + order form (Fjord)

Marissa / Karthik — this is very helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from Fjord legal / procurement:

- The output ownership clause you proposed matches our expectation. Please include the exact language in the MSA redline that we can circulate internally (we need copy/pasteable text).
- Training opt-in via Order Form is acceptable; we do want an express reference in the Order Form that checks the box and attaches the SOW that lists data types and retention.
- On telemetry: acceptable to provide aggregated metrics, but please add a short definition of "aggregated, non-identifiable" in the MSA to avoid future disputes.
- Procurement would like SOC 2 and a short runbook describing incident escalation and data deletion timelines before we get to signature.

Assuming the tracked MSA we received has the exact output ownership language and the Order Form opt-in mechanism, Procurement is prepared to move to counter-signature week of Aug 6. We'll hold off public procurement approvals until we see the final tracked redline.

I'll loop Aaron in for any legal-level tweaks; thanks for turning this around quickly.

—Emma
